title: IAM Features.Validate() enforces API dependency invariants
answers: Why does enabling serviceaccounttokens in iam apis config fail validation?
What enforces IAM API dependency rules at startup?
Where do I add a new required-API dependency for an IAM feature?
body:
Symptom: enabling service account tokens or service-account resource permissions via explicit startup config silently has no effect or is inconsistent.
Root cause: those sub-features depend on a parent API being enabled but nothing enforced it before explicit startup config existed.
Fix pattern: Features.Validate() (pkg/registry/apis/iam/features.go) centrally checks cross-API dependencies (ServiceAccountTokensAPI requires ServiceAccountsAPI; ServiceAccountResourcePermissions requires ResourcePermissionsAPI) and returns an error if violated.
Constraints: any new IAM API that is only meaningful alongside another API must add its dependency check here; this validation only runs for the explicit-config path, not the legacy per-flag OpenFeature path.
applies: pkg/registry/apis/iam/features.go Features.Validate when an IAM sub-feature requires another API
